questions: Which feature of the cactus solves the problem of having no water?
Did the cactus choose to grow its thorns? How do you know?
segments.say: Watch out: features are not grown by choice. Watch the cactus in the hot, dry desert: its thick stem stores water like a bottle, its sharp thorns stop thirsty animals from biting it, and its deep roots reach down to find water. Hold up the warning in the caption - these features fit the desert perfectly, but they were not grown by choice. Keep your student notes open at the adaptation definition for this scene.

questions: Why can the hungry bird not spot the moth?
What is the special word for blending in with your home?
segments.say: Blending in keeps animals safe. Look hard at the tree bark and try to spot the moth before the arrow points to it: its wings are the same colour as the bark, so it blends in and the hungry bird flies right past. Matching its home is called camouflage. Now try the cactus and camouflage questions on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: Why do the birds leave when winter comes?
When will the birds come back, and what brings them back?
segments.say: Birds travel far to survive. Trace the route arrow as the flock flies south: winter is coming, food is hard to find, so the birds fly thousands of kilometres to warmer places to survive. This yearly journey is migration, and the birds return when spring brings food back. Check this against the migration definition in your student notes.

questions: What is left standing after the forest is cleared?
What do the forest animals lose when the trees go?
segments.say: People change animal homes. Watch the forest trees disappear one by one as people clear the land for farms and roads, and follow the monkey as it moves away: when the trees go, the animals lose their food and shelter. Then finish by taking the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly the feature-choice trap from scene s1.
segments.watchFor: An animal can decide to grow a new feature when it needs one. Listen and look for it in pair talk and on the exit ticket: The feature fits the animal so well that it looks chosen on purpose. Send them back to scene s1 and to the correct turn: These features did not appear overnight: they developed over many, many generations, not by choice.
